newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends sharply down on LME losses.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends sharply down on LME losses.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended sharply down on Tuesday on overnight heavy losses on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at 22,830 yuan (2,752) per tonne, losing 620 yuan. It opened at 22,800 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 22,770 and a high of 22,960.
April fell 360 yuan to 22,960, May 400 to 22,910, June 470 to 22,930, August 600 to 22,850, September 650 to 22,800 and October 650 to 22,800.
Combined volume rose sharply to 113,660 tonnes from 40,550.
Copper opened sharply lower and moved at low levels for most of the session.
Traders said overnight LME losses triggered panic selling.
"Panic stop loss orders dominated today's trading with most investors pessimistic about the short-term market trend," one trader said.
"LME losses made most Shanghai long positon holders give up," a second trader said.
Most analysts said they expected copper to fall further in the next few days.
Aluminium followed copper's trend. April fell 250 to 15,350 yuan per tonne, May 290 to 15,400, June 310 to 15,640 and July 350 to 15,800.
Combined volume fell to 3,840 tonnes from 3,880.
